what_its_for: Frovatriptan is used to treat migraine headaches in adults. It helps relieve the pain, nausea, and sensitivity to light and sound that come with migraines. It is NOT used to prevent migraines or treat other types of headaches like tension headaches or cluster headaches.
how_to_take: Take frovatriptan by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Take it as soon as you notice your migraine starting. If your headache comes back after getting better, you may take a second dose at least 2 hours after the first dose. Do not take more than 3 tablets (7.5 mg total) in any 24-hour period.
dosing: The usual dose is one 2.5 mg tablet taken at the first sign of a migraine. If the headache returns, a second 2.5 mg tablet may be taken at least 2 hours after the first. The maximum dose in 24 hours is 3 tablets (7.5 mg). Do not use this medicine to treat more than 4 migraines per month without talking to your doctor.
missed_dose: Frovatriptan is only taken when you have a migraine, not on a regular daily schedule. There is no such thing as a missed dose. Never take a double dose to make up for one you forgot.
storage: Store frovatriptan at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep it in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking frovatriptan within 24 hours of another triptan medicine (such as sumatriptan or rizatriptan) or an ergotamine-type medicine (such as ergotamine or dihydroergotamine). Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, as it may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Limit or avoid alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can worsen headaches. Avoid smoking, as it may increase your risk of heart-related side effects.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek emergency help right away if you experience: chest pain, tightness, pressure, or heaviness in the chest, throat, neck, or jaw; sudden severe headache different from your usual migraine; shortness of breath; fast or irregular heartbeat; sudden numbness or weakness on one side of your body; sudden vision changes or trouble speaking; signs of a stroke; severe stomach pain; skin rash, hives, or swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat; or if your migraine is not getting better after taking the medicine. Also call your doctor if you need to use this medicine more than 10 days per month, as overuse can make headaches worse.
when_it_works: Frovatriptan usually starts to relieve migraine pain within 2 hours of taking it. Because frovatriptan stays in the body longer than some other triptans, it may have a lower chance of the headache coming back. However, it may work more slowly than other triptans, so take it at the very first sign of a migraine for best results.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Elderly patients (over 65): This medicine has not been well studied in patients over 65 years old. Use with caution and only as directed by your doctor. Kidney or liver problems: Use with caution. This medicine has not been studied in people with severe kidney or liver disease, so tell your doctor if you have these conditions. Children: Frovatriptan is not approved for use in patients under 18 years of age. Heart disease risk: Do not use this medicine if you have a history of heart disease, uncontrolled high blood pressure, stroke, or circulation problems without first talking to your doctor.
